{{Quote|With the old Sullustan Dua Ningo in charge of the armada, the Bulwark Fleet broke through the Republic's blockade and proceeded to smash military outposts throughout Coruscant's Sector Zero.|''The New Essential Chronology'', on the Battle of Foerost|<ref name="NEC" />}}
'''Dua Ningo''' was an elder [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] who served as an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] in the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|navy]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. In [[20 BBY/Legends|20.1 BBY]], about two [[Standard year/Legends|years]] into the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Ningo took command of the [[Bulwark Fleet]], an [[Fleet/Legends|armada]] of [[Bulwark Mark I]] [[Warship/Legends|warships]]. After [[Battle of Foerost (Clone Wars)|breaking]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]], Ningo wiped out many Republic outposts in [[Imperial Center Oversector|Sector Zero]] as he moved to conquer the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] planet of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Hoping to put an end to Ningo's [[Foerost campaign|campaign]], the Republic authorized the launch of the new [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyers]] and engaged Ningo and his Bulwark Fleet in a series of battles throughout the Core. The [[Battle of Anaxes (21 BBY)|final confrontation]] between the two armadas occurred in the skies above the Core World [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], where the admiral was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when his [[Unrepentant (Bulwark Mark I)|flagship]] disintegrated.

==Biography==
{{Quote|The final showdown came in the skies above Anaxes. Dodonna, under heavy fire with dead wrecks from his task force plunging planetward, held out long enough for Screed to pop in from hyperspace and disintegrate Ningo's flagship with a broadside fusillade.|''The New Essential Chronology'', on the Battle of Anaxes|<ref name="NEC" />}}
Dua Ningo served as an [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]]<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> in the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|naval forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict known as the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="CSWE" /> In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], Ningo assumed the leadership of the [[Bulwark Fleet]], an [[Fleet/Legends|armada]] of [[Bulwark Mark I]] [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] that had been constructed by [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] at the [[Foerost Shipyards]], and used the [[Warship/Legends|warships]] to [[Battle of Foerost (Clone Wars)|defeat]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of<ref name="NEC" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> [[Foerost/Legends|Foerost]].<ref name="NEC" /> Following this historic<ref name="Atlas" /> victory, the admiral was tasked with conquering the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] planet of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="CSWE" /> destroying a series of Republic outposts in [[Imperial Center Oversector|Sector Zero]] en route.<ref name="NEC" />

[[File:VSD-SWR.png|thumb|300px|right|The Republic utilized ''Victory I''-class Star Destroyers to combat Ningo and his forces.]]
Recognizing the threat that Ningo posed, the Republic authorized the launch of the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class Star Destroyer]], a new warship design, six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] prior to its scheduled debut in order to deal with the Bulwark Fleet. Two [[Task force/Legends|task forces]] of ''Victory''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]]&mdash;collectively known as the [[Victory Fleet]]&mdash;were formed: one led by [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Terrinald Screed/Legends|Terrinald Screed]] and the other by Captain [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]].<ref name="NEC" /> The Victory Fleet succeeded in driving Ningo away from Coruscant,<ref name="CSWE" /> subsequently engaging him in a [[Foerost campaign|series of battles]] throughout the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="NEC" />

Ningo survived encounters with the Victory Fleet above<ref name="CSWE" /> the planets<ref name="EGW" /><ref name="Ixtlar">{{CSWECite|II|126|Ixtlar}}</ref> [[Battle of Ixtlar (Clone Wars)|Ixtlar]], [[Battle of Alsakan (Clone Wars)|Alsakan]], and [[Battle of Basilisk (Clone Wars)|Basilisk]], before moving the Bulwark Fleet to the planet [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]]. There, the admiral succeeded in [[Battle of Anaxes (21 BBY)|destroying]] a large portion of Dodonna's task force, but Ningo's concentration on one [[Commander/Legends|commander]] left him vulnerable to attack from the other&mdash;Screed and his warships emerged from [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and destroyed the admiral's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]],<ref name="CSWE" /> the [[Unrepentant (Bulwark Mark I)|''Unrepentant'']],<ref name="EGW" /> in a barrage of [[Laser cannon/Legends|cannon]] fire.<ref name="NEC" /> Ningo [[Death/Legends|perished]] when his ship was obliterated.<ref name="CSWE" /> Dua Ningo was eventually mentioned in [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|''The New Essential Chronology'']], a historical chronicle compiled by the [[Historical Council]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and released in [[36 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" />

==Personality and traits==
Dua Ningo was a [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]]<ref name="CSWE" /> who was considered old by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the Clone Wars.<ref name="NEC" /> Serving as a Confederacy of Independent Systems admiral,<ref name="CSWE" /> the Galactic Republic government considered the admiral and his forces to be such a threat that it launched its new ''Victory''-class Star Destroyers months in advance of their planned rollout to deal with the Bulwark Fleet and its commander.<ref name="NEC" />

==Behind the scenes==
Dua Ningo was first mentioned in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', a reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and published in [[2005]].<ref name="NEC" />
